368305.title: Bensmail–Mc Inerney's vertex-capturing game conjecture
368305.literal_statement:
For the vertex-capturing game $\operatorname{VC}(n)$ on the complete graph $K_n$, let $s_{\operatorname{VC}}(n)$ denote the optimal score difference between the two players.

**Bensmail–Mc Inerney's conjecture.**

$$
s_{\operatorname{VC}}(n)=\begin{cases} 2 & \text{if } n=2\\ 1 & \text{if } n\equiv 3 \pmod 4\\ 0 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}
$$

The source attributes this conjecture to Bensmail and Mc Inerney and states that it was confirmed for $n\leq 6$; its general status is not resolved in the supplied text.

368305.disposition: The source (arXiv:2505.03497) already extends the original n <= 6 check to n <= 8 by computer and to n <= 9 via its Proposition 5 (n = 3 mod 4 implies n = 1 mod 4). The next open case n = 10 is a 45-edge positional game on K_10; even with S_10 symmetry the position space (about 3^45/10!) is far beyond the lane caps in Python. No structural reduction found beyond the source.

318027.title: The regular Ramsey number comparison conjecture
318027.literal_statement:
Let $R(k,\ell)$ be the Ramsey number, and let $R^{\mathrm{reg}}(k,\ell)$ denote the corresponding Ramsey number restricted to regular graphs. **Regular Ramsey comparison conjecture.** For every $k\geq 2$ there is a constant $c_k>0$ such that

$$
R^{\mathrm{reg}}(k,\ell)\geq c_k R(k,\ell)
$$

for all $\ell\geq 2$. This conjecture proposes that regularity changes Ramsey numbers by at most a constant factor for each fixed $k$; the source presents it as a plausible natural question, with no resolution indicated.

367549.title: The boundedness conjecture for gluing posets
367549.literal_statement: Let $\mathcal P_1$ and $\mathcal P_2$ be finite posets with bounded saturation number, and let $\mathcal P_2*\mathcal P_1$ denote their gluing, obtained by placing every element of $\mathcal P_1$ below every element of $\mathcal P_2$. Let $\operatorname{sat}^*(n,\mathcal P)$ denote the induced saturation number. **Gluing-boundedness conjecture.** The glued poset $\mathcal P_2*\mathcal P_1$ also has bounded saturation number. This is a special case of the preceding unboundedness conjecture and is presented as a desired extension of the paper's boundedness theorem to arbitrary posets.

367669.title: Generic small-time null-controllability conjecture for the heat equation on graphs
367669.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a graph with $N$ edges $(e_i)_{i=1,\dots,N}$ and let $\omega$ be an open subset of $\mathcal{G}$. The lengths of the edges are $(\ell_i)_{i=1,\dots,N}$.

**Generic heat-control conjecture.** Generically with respect to the lengths $(\ell_i)_{i=1,\dots,N}$, the heat equation is small-time null-controllable.

The claim is presented as a natural extension of the stated result for generic star graphs, where small-time null-controllability holds for every $T>0$. Its validity for more general graph structures remains open.

367666.title: Avdonin–Zhao's watershed conjecture for optimal graph control time
367666.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a metric graph, and let the free wave equation on $\mathcal{G}$ be observed or controlled from an open subset of the graph. A watershed is the decomposition used by Avdonin and Zhao to determine a control time from the longest river covering the uncontrolled part.

**Avdonin–Zhao's watershed conjecture.** The watershed description of Avdonin and Zhao provides the optimal time for the observation and control of the free wave equation on a graph.

Computing the optimal observation and control time on a general graph is described as an open problem. The watershed time is always shorter than the time obtained from the graph geometric control condition, but its optimality is not known in general.

primary.statement_excerpt:
Conjecture 7.1.



The watershed description of Avdonin and Zhao in [13] provides the optimal time for the observation and control of the free wave equation on a graph.





7.2 On the (possible) minimal time for the Schrödinger equation




In Theorem 1.11, we exhibit a specific configuration where the Schrödinger equation turns out to be exactly controllable for some  T>0  despite (GGCC) is not satisfied. A natural question would consist in investigating if there is indeed a minimal time of control or not. Actually, based on our experience on the subject of the internal control of linear Schrödinger equation where as far as we know, minimal time never appears, we conjecture the following.



Conjecture 7.2.



Let us consider the X graph with four edges, two (say  e_{1}  and  e_{2} ) of length  \ell_{\text{b}}>0  and two ( e_{3}  and  e_{4} ), of length  \ell_{\text{t}}>0  and  \omega=e_{1}\cup e_{3} . Assume that the ratio  \ell_{\text{t}}/\ell_{\text{b}}  is a badly approximable number then the Schrödinger equation




 \left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}i\partial_{t}u=-\Delta_{\mathcal{G}}u+h1_{\omega},&\ \ \ \ t>0,\\
u(t=0)=u_{0}\in L^{2}(\mathcal{G}),&\end{array}\right. 

(59)


is small-time exactly controllable in  L^{2}(\mathcal{G}) .

373770.title: Banica–Bichon's maximality conjecture for classical permutation groups
373770.statement: Let $S_N$ be the classical permutation group and $S_N^+$ Wang's quantum permutation group, with $S_N\leq S_N^+$ denoting the inclusion as a quantum subgroup. **The Maximality Conjecture.** The quantum subgroup $S_N\leq S_N^+$ is maximal at all $N$. This conjecture extends the known result for $N=4$ and asks whether the classical permutation group is maximal inside the quantum permutation group for every parameter $N$; the supplied source gives no resolution beyond the stated small-parameter progress.
